title: Feynman's 'Any Questions?' teaching at a Buffalo aerospace company, and his nuclear patents

tellings.quote: Do you remember a story called Any Questions in which he goes to Buffalo, New York because as a physics professor at Cornell, he has to teach in an aerospace company.

plain: The physicist Richard Feynman told a story called "Any Questions?" about having to travel to Buffalo, New York, while a physics professor at Cornell University, to teach at an aerospace company. A researcher named Eric Weinstein brings it up from Feynman's memoir books, Surely You're Joking, Mr. Feynman! and What Do You Care What Other People Think?, and ties it to patents Feynman held on nuclear technology. To Weinstein it shows how closely top physicists were tied to military industry.
